bug_description.normalized: The staged 86-byte UART witness is a single HDLC frame. After HDLC decode and FCS removal, the Spinel payload begins `cf 03 73 4d 00 ...`: `PROP_VALUE_SET` with packed property key `0x73`, so `CommandHandler_PROP_VALUE_update()` dispatches to `HandlePropertySet<SPINEL_PROP_STREAM_NET_INSECURE>`. That handler then reads a 77-byte IPv6 packet whose hop-by-hop option bytes are `20 00 20 00 20 00 20 00 20 00 6d 09 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00`. The raw-send path reparses that packet, sees that its destination is not one of the node's own addresses and is not link-local, and therefore processes the existing MPL option as forwardable traffic. MPL buffers a clone with outbound retransmission metadata (`transmissionCount = 1`). Because the harness already forced the node into leader mode, MPL timer expirations are `2`; the first retransmission timer tick therefore removes the metadata trailer from the buffered packet and re-enqueues that packet to `Ip6::HandleSendQueue()`, which re-enters `HandleDatagram()` with `aFromNcpHost = false`. `ProcessReceiveCallback()` then clones the packet for host delivery and calls `RemoveMplOption()`. `RemoveMplOption()` copies the crafted MPL option length byte `0x09` into `mplLength` but lacks the fixed commit's bound check `mplLength <= sizeof(OptionMpl) - sizeof(OptionHeader)`. Because the MPL option is preceded by five skip options and followed by Pad1, it is neither the first-and-only option nor the last 8 bytes of the hop-by-hop header, so the function falls into the PadN replacement path and calls `padOption.Init(sizeof(OptionHeader) + mplLength)`, i.e. `Init(11)`. `OptionPadN::Init()` then executes `memset(mPad, kData, 9)` on the 5-byte `mPad` array inside the 7-byte packed stack object `padOption`, matching the reproduced ASan WRITE of size 9 and overflowing 4 bytes beyond `padOption`.

source.description: First project-side consumption of attacker-controlled input into vulnerability-relevant state. This decodes the packed Spinel property key byte into `propKey`, which selects the later crashing `STREAM_NET_INSECURE` handler.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is an 86-byte HDLC frame delimited by `0x7e`. After HDLC decode and 2-byte FCS removal, the single Spinel frame begins `cf 03 73 4d 00 ...`: header `0xcf`, command `SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_SET (0x03)`, packed property key byte `0x73`, then little-endian value length `0x004d`. `ReadUintPacked(propKey)` therefore returns `SPINEL_PROP_STREAM_NET_INSECURE`, and the remaining property value is a 77-byte IPv6 packet whose hop-by-hop option bytes are `20 00 20 00 20 00 20 00 20 00 6d 09 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment copies the attacker-controlled MPL option length byte into `mplLength`. For the witness bytes `6d 09`, `mplLength` becomes `9`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `RemoveMplOption()` trusts the attacker-supplied MPL length byte and does not apply the fixed commit's upper-bound check `mplLength <= sizeof(OptionMpl) - sizeof(OptionHeader)` before using that value to size `OptionPadN`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `OptionPadN::Init()` writes 9 bytes into the 5-byte `mPad` array inside the 7-byte packed stack object `padOption`; the first 5 bytes fill `mPad` and the remaining 4 bytes overflow past `padOption`, matching ASan's WRITE of size 9.

parser_admitted.description: After `CommandHandler_PROP_VALUE_update()` decodes property key `0x73`, `FindSetPropertyHandler()` resolves it to `HandlePropertySet<SPINEL_PROP_STREAM_NET_INSECURE>`, and this indirect call enters that handler instead of rejecting the frame.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness initializes OpenThread, forces the instance into leader mode, feeds the staged 86-byte UART witness to `otPlatUartReceived`, and then processes tasklets and timers.
The UART bytes HDLC-decode into one Spinel frame; framing and FCS are removed and the resulting payload begins `cf 03 73 4d 00 ...`.
Spinel parsing decodes property key `0x73` (`SPINEL_PROP_STREAM_NET_INSECURE`) and dispatches the command into the insecure network-stream set handler.
The selected handler reads a 77-byte IPv6 datagram from the property value, wraps those bytes in an `otMessage`, and hands that packet to raw IPv6 send processing.

Raw IPv6 handling treats the crafted packet as forwardable, MPL buffers it with outbound retransmission metadata, and the first leader-mode retransmission timer expiry removes the metadata trailer and re-enqueues the buffered packet to `Ip6::HandleSendQueue()` with `aFromNcpHost=false`.

Host-delivery processing clones the retransmitted packet and tries to replace the MPL option with `PadN`; unchecked `mplLength = 9` becomes `padOption.Init(11)`, and `OptionPadN::Init()` performs a 9-byte write into the 5-byte `mPad` array inside the 7-byte stack object `padOption`, overflowing 4 bytes beyond the object.

fine_trace.note: Source. This decodes the next packed Spinel integer byte `0x73` into `propKey`, producing the dispatch key that selects the vulnerable handler.
The decoded property key hits the `SPINEL_PROP_STREAM_NET_INSECURE` switch arm, resolving dispatch to the insecure network-stream setter.

Inside the selected handler, this reads the property's length-prefixed value into `framePtr/frameLen`. For the witness, that value is a 77-byte IPv6 packet whose hop-by-hop option bytes are `20 00 20 00 20 00 20 00 20 00 6d 09 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00`.
The handler wraps the 77 attacker-controlled bytes in an `otMessage`, preserving the crafted IPv6 header and existing MPL option for later raw-send parsing.

In the first `SendRaw()` pass, `IsUnicastAddress(header.GetDestination())` is false for this non-local destination and `header.GetDestination().IsLinkLocal()` is also false, so the packet is marked for forwarding.

While parsing the hop-by-hop header, MPL processing reaches the witness option type `0x6d` and, on the fresh instance, accepts its seed/sequence and enters `AddBufferedMessage()` with `aIsOutbound = true`.
MPL clones the packet, sets `transmissionCount` to `1` because `aIsOutbound` is true, appends that retransmission metadata to the clone, and enqueues the buffered clone in `mBufferedMessageSet`.

Leader mode set `mTimerExpirations = 2` before the input was delivered. On the first retransmission timer expiry, the buffered message's `transmissionCount` increments from `1` to `2`, satisfying the final retransmission branch; `messageMetadata.RemoveFrom(*message)` strips the trailer and the original buffered packet is enqueued onto `Ip6`'s send queue.
The retransmission copy re-enters IPv6 handling from the send queue with the literal `false` `aFromNcpHost` argument, unlike the original `SendRaw()` call that used `true`.

This host-origin guard now passes. NCP initialization already installed a non-null receive callback at `src/ncp/ncp_base.cpp:267`, so `ProcessReceiveCallback()` continues to clone the packet and call `RemoveMplOption()` on the clone instead of dropping the traffic.

Tainted length origin and root cause. When `RemoveMplOption()` reaches the witness MPL header `6d 09`, it records the option start offset and copies the attacker-controlled length byte `0x09` into `mplLength`. The vulnerable commit does not bound-check `mplLength` before later using it as a PadN size.

fine_trace.code: if (mplOffset == sizeof(ip6Header) + sizeof(hbh) && hbh.GetLength() == 0) { ... } else if (mplOffset + 8 == endOffset) { ... }
fine_trace.note: The packet layout defeats both removal cases. `hbh.GetLength()` is `2`, five preceding `20 00` skip options place the MPL option at offset `52`, and the trailing Pad1 leaves `endOffset = 64`, so neither the first-and-only check nor the `mplOffset + 8 == endOffset` check holds. `remove` therefore stays false while `mplOffset != 0`.

Because execution falls into the `else if (mplOffset != 0)` replacement path, the code derives `aPadLength = sizeof(OptionHeader) + mplLength = 2 + 9 = 11` from the unchecked attacker-controlled length and passes that oversized PadN length into `OptionPadN::Init()`.

Sink. `OptionPadN` is a packed 7-byte object: the 2-byte `OptionHeader` plus the 5-byte `mPad` array. `Init(11)` therefore makes `memset(mPad, kData, 9)` write 9 bytes starting at `mPad`: 5 bytes land in `mPad` and the remaining 4 bytes overflow past the end of stack `padOption`, matching ASan's `WRITE of size 9`.

format.name: OpenThread NCP UART STREAM_NET_INSECURE MPL witness
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly 86 bytes and must remain a single HDLC frame. After HDLC decode and FCS removal, it must yield one Spinel `PROP_VALUE_SET` frame beginning `cf 03 73 4d 00 ...`: packed property key `0x73` (`SPINEL_PROP_STREAM_NET_INSECURE`), then a 77-byte IPv6 packet and empty metadata. That IPv6 packet must carry hop-by-hop option bytes `20 00 20 00 20 00 20 00 20 00 6d 09 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00`, so `RemoveMplOption()` later reads `mplLength = 9`, leaves `remove` false, and calls `OptionPadN::Init(11)`.
